style: Bengal Navaratna and Classical Terracotta architecture
key_structures: Carved brick terracotta friezes depicting Puranic narratives
special_features: Distinctive Navaratna (nine-pinnacled) terracotta temple design representing traditional Bengal architectural heights
Revered as the historical Pradyumna-mandala of ancient Rarh Bengal
Historical site preserved through local devotee resilience and memory
renovation_history: Original temple described in ancient texts fell during medieval invasions (around 14th century); worshipped in local sanctums in Pandua/Hooghly; renovated by regional Shakta devotees.
